text:
Stale Food, Sour Coffee & Zero Quality Control. I had a very disappointing experience ordering from Swish.

The chicken popcorn was completely unacceptable. The portion size was far smaller than expected, and the quality was even worse. It tasted stale, as if it had been sitting around for a long time, and it seemed like it had simply been reheated from frozen instead of being freshly prepared. The texture was chewy and unpleasant, making it inedible.

The coffee was equally disappointing. The milk used tasted stale, which gave the coffee a distinctly sour taste. Fresh milk is a basic expectation, so receiving a beverage that tasted spoiled was very concerning.

The lemon iced tea was another letdown. It was overwhelmingly sweet, to the point where the lemon flavor was barely noticeable. On top of that, it had a strange aftertaste that made it difficult to drink.

Overall, every item in the order had a quality issue. For a food delivery service, freshness and consistency should be the minimum standard. This experience fell well below expectations, and I hope Swish takes quality control more seriously because customers should not be paying for stale food and poorly prepared beverages.
title: Stale Food, Sour Coffee & Zero Quality Control

A Loyal Customer’s Appreciation and Sustainability Request. I’ve been using Swish for quite a long time now, and I must say I’m really happy with the overall experience. The deliveries are extremely quick, the prices are affordable, and the service is reliable.

One thing I particularly like is that the app offers a limited and carefully selected range of products. Unlike many other platforms that can feel overwhelming and confusing, Swish keeps things simple, clear, and easy to navigate. The delivery timings are also very convenient and consistently well-managed.

As a frequent customer who has placed many orders over time, I’ve accumulated a large number of the paper bags/packages that come with the deliveries. This got me thinking about a sustainability initiative that Swish could consider. It would be wonderful if the company introduced a program where customers could return the used paper bags and packaging materials for reuse or recycling. I’m not looking for any reward, money, or benefits in return—I simply don’t like the idea of throwing them away when they could potentially be reused.

I believe this could be a great eco-friendly initiative that benefits both customers and the environment. It would be amazing to see Swish take a step in this direction and encourage sustainable packaging practices.

Overall, a fantastic app with excellent service. Keep up the great work!

Quick Feedback From a Fellow Developer. 1. When a product is added and the bottom add-to-cart drawer is open, switching to another app and returning causes the drawer to appear half-expanded with the background greyed out and the screen becoming non-interactive instead of restoring or closing properly.

2. In the product description, there is a “—” (dash separator) appearing in the text, which looks like AI-generated or placeholder formatting and feels out of place in the UI copy.
Product name :Salted Popcorn

3. While adding items to the cart, the quantity is restricted to a maximum of 3, after which a toast message appears saying “Maximum limit reached for this item,” but the limit is not communicated beforehand on the product UI, which may confuse users.

4. In the cart section, when using the “Add items to unlock deals” feature, the bottom drawer allows increasing item quantity up to 3, but when tapping the “+” icon again, the quantity does not increase and no toast message (“Maximum limit reached for this item”) is shown, unlike the normal product flow. This creates inconsistent behavior and missing user feedback.

5. There is a homepage banner stating “Get free peri peri potato wedges on orders above 349”, When the cart value crosses the offer threshold, the free item (Peri Peri Wedges) appears under Freebies. However, if the user taps Remove, the free item disappears and there is no way to add it back again, even though the cart value is still above the eligibility amount. Increasing quantity or adding more products does not restore the freebie option.

6. The veg indicator icon is consistent across regular cart items, but in the Freebies section (Peri Peri Wedges) the veg icon style/size appears different, causing a visual inconsistency in the cart UI.

Overall, the app experience is really good. The UI looks clean, modern, and well thought out. The UX flow is smooth in most areas, and the design quality stands out. The above points are just observations to help make an already good product even more polished.

Adnan Sami
